title: Chicken Caesar Salad
shortDescription: Crispy chicken, real parmesan, crew salad night
subtitle: Crispy chicken, real parmesan, crew salad night
description: Big bowls, hot chicken, all the fixings. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep romaine and dressing station
steps.instruction: Chop romaine hearts into bite-sized pieces; wash and spin dry — wet lettuce rejects dressing. Shave parmesan into a bowl. Set Caesar dressing, croutons, and lemon wedges in labeled containers before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.instruction: Lay thick-cut bacon on sheet pans in a single layer. Bake at 400°F 15–18 minutes until shatter-crisp and deep mahogany. Drain on paper towels; crumble when cool. Hold warm in a dry pan — wet bacon steams the salad.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.instruction: Heat a grill pan or flat-top over medium-high until a water drop sizzles. Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Cook 5–6 minutes per side until deep grill marks show and thickest part reads 160°F. Rest 5 minutes tented with foil.

steps.title: Verify chicken at 165°F
steps.instruction: Slice rested chicken across the grain and probe the center of the thickest piece — must read 165°F before it hits the salad line. Any pink or under-temp slice goes back to the grill 2 minutes per side. Hold sliced chicken loosely covered at 140°F.

steps.title: Bake garlic bread
steps.instruction: Spread garlic butter on halved baguettes edge to edge. Bake at 400°F 8–10 minutes until edges are crisp and tops golden — garlic burns fast, so watch the last 2 minutes. Slice on a bias and hold in a warm pan.

steps.title: Toast the croutons
steps.instruction: Toss day-old bread cubes with olive oil, salt, and garlic powder. Spread on a sheet pan and bake at 400°F 8–10 minutes until crunchy through the center — soft cores sog out dressed romaine in minutes.

steps.title: Bake diner fries (optional)
steps.instruction: Spread frozen fries in a single layer on sheet pans. Bake at 425°F 20–22 minutes until deeply golden with audible crunch when shaken. Season with salt immediately out of the oven; hold in a warm pan with the door cracked.

steps.title: Toss the Caesar
steps.instruction: Toss dried romaine with dressing gradually — coated leaves, not soup. Fold in half the parmesan, croutons, and crumbled bacon. Add dressing in two passes so bowls stay crisp until the crew hits the line.

steps.title: Plate hot chicken over salad
steps.instruction: Lay warm sliced chicken over the dressed romaine in hotel pans or individual bowls. Finish with remaining parmesan, bacon, and a lemon squeeze at the table. Garlic bread and fries go on separate trays.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover grilled chicken — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool grilled chicken and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Slice chicken thick and against the grain so it feels like a main, not a garnish.
Dress each bowl to order — soggy Caesar kills the vibe.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F during rest — dry breast ruins crew morale.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Sides: garlic bread, croutons, crispy bacon, shaved parmesan, optional diner fries
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool grilled chicken in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Store dressed salad separately from chicken — acid wilts romaine overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Crispy chicken, real parmesan, crew salad night. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
